label: Wrong variant shipped
agent_action_log: User instructed: 'buy wireless earbuds under $100 with good reviews'
Agent searched merchant catalog, selected X200 (4.6 stars, $89.99)
Agent completed checkout autonomously via ACP, no user confirmation step triggered (below $100 auto-approve threshold)
dispute_reason: Buyer received item but says color (black) does not match what listing implied (product photo showed white variant as default)
gold_rationale: Listing ambiguity is a merchant-side error, not buyer or agent error. Replace with correct variant at no cost; no policy violation by the purchasing agent.

label: Charged twice
agent_action_log: User instructed: 'buy wireless earbuds under $100 with good reviews'
Agent purchased same item twice within 40 seconds due to a retry-on-timeout bug in the agent's checkout tool call
No duplicate-order confirmation was surfaced to user
dispute_reason: Buyer was charged twice for a single requested purchase
gold_rationale: Duplicate charge caused by a purchasing-agent tool-call bug, not a user decision. Full refund of the duplicate transaction; no restocking fee applies since merchant is not at fault but buyer should not bear agent error cost.

label: No-returns policy
agent_action_log: User instructed: 'find a housewarming gift around $150, something unique, ship to my sister'
Agent selected vase from a small-batch artisan seller, final-sale item per merchant policy (clearly marked in listing)
Agent completed purchase; final-sale terms were included in the tool's structured listing data but not surfaced to the user before purchase
dispute_reason: Buyer wants to return the item because the sister already owns a similar vase; merchant's listed policy is final-sale, no returns
gold_rationale: Merchant policy is unambiguous and was available to the agent pre-purchase (procedural compliance), but the agent failed to surface a material term (final-sale) before an irreversible action. This is a borderline case involving agent disclosure failure vs. legitimate merchant policy — route to human review rather than auto-deciding either way.

label: Agent missed price guardrail
agent_action_log: User instructed: 'set up a recurring order for my usual protein powder, cancel if price goes up more than 10%'
Agent set up subscription per user's stated price-increase cancellation rule
Merchant raised price by 18% for the August billing cycle
Agent did not detect the price change and allowed the renewal to proceed
dispute_reason: Buyer was charged at a price 18% above their stated cancellation threshold; agent failed to monitor and cancel per explicit instruction
gold_rationale: Clear violation of an explicit user-set policy guardrail by the purchasing agent. Refund the price difference (or full renewal amount per platform's standing policy) and flag the agent's price-monitoring tool as defective.

label: Changed my mind
agent_action_log: User instructed: 'buy me a 40L hiking backpack, nothing over $150'
Agent selected backpack within budget from a verified merchant
User received the correct item as described, no error in listing or agent behavior
dispute_reason: Buyer simply changed their mind and no longer wants the backpack; requests refund citing standard 30-day return window
gold_rationale: No agent or merchant error occurred. This is a standard buyer's-remorse return within the merchant's stated 30-day window — process under normal return policy, unrelated to any agentic-purchase failure mode.

label: Bundle item defective

transaction.item: Home office bundle (desk lamp, cable organizer, USB hub)

agent_action_log: User instructed: 'get me a basic home office bundle under $100'
Agent purchased a 3-item bundle from a single listing (desk lamp, cable organizer, USB hub)
Agent completed checkout autonomously via ACP; bundle is sold as a single non-separable SKU per merchant listing
dispute_reason: The USB hub in the bundle arrived dead on arrival; the other two items work fine. Buyer wants the hub fixed or replaced, not the whole bundle.
gold_rationale: Manufacturing defect on one component of a multi-item purchase is a standard merchant-side quality issue. Replace only the defective component (or the smallest replaceable unit the merchant supports); no need to touch the working items or escalate.

label: Unexpected customs fee
agent_action_log: User instructed: 'find a nice pour-over coffee set, budget around $60'
Agent selected an item from an international merchant (ships from EU); listing's structured data included an import-duty disclosure field
Agent completed purchase without relaying the import-duty disclosure to the user before checkout
dispute_reason: Buyer was charged a $14 customs/import fee on delivery that they say they were never told about
gold_rationale: The import-duty term was present and legitimate in the merchant's listing data at time of purchase — this is a real, disclosed cost of international shipping, not a merchant error or a policy violation. The agent's failure to proactively surface it is a UX gap worth logging, but it does not entitle the buyer to a refund of a legitimate customs charge; deny the dispute and note the disclosure gap separately.

label: High-value wrong item

transaction.item: Carbon road bike frame, size M

agent_action_log: User instructed: 'buy the carbon frame from Summit Cycle Supply, size medium, budget up to $400'
Agent selected the listed size-medium carbon frame and completed checkout via ACP
Merchant's fulfillment system shipped a size-large frame instead of the ordered medium — a warehouse picking error on the merchant's side
dispute_reason: Buyer received the wrong frame size entirely; wants a refund or the correct item
gold_rationale: The fault is unambiguous (merchant warehouse error), but the transaction amount ($340) exceeds the guardrail threshold. Per the escalation guardrail, high-dollar cases route to human review regardless of how clear-cut the fault determination is — the agent's suggested decision (replace) should still be produced as a recommendation for the reviewer.

label: Conflicting instructions
agent_action_log: User instructed: 'buy a bluetooth speaker, something waterproof'
Agent selected a speaker marked water-resistant (not fully waterproof) — closest match available under budget
Agent's log does not record whether it flagged the water-resistant vs. waterproof distinction to the user before purchase
dispute_reason: Buyer says they explicitly told the agent (in a prior conversation turn not captured in this transaction's action log) that the item had to be fully waterproof, not just water-resistant, and that the agent should have refused to buy this item
gold_rationale: The action log doesn't clearly establish fault: it's undetermined whether the agent ignored a real constraint or the buyer is misremembering an instruction that was never actually given. This is a genuinely unclear fault hypothesis, not just a low-confidence policy match — it should escalate to human review regardless of the transaction amount, since no policy lookup can resolve a factual dispute about what instruction was actually given.

label: Subscription not cancelled
agent_action_log: User instructed on 2026-07-10: 'cancel my protein powder subscription, I don't need it anymore'
Agent logged the cancellation request but the cancellation tool call failed silently (no retry, no error surfaced to user)
Subscription renewed and charged again on 2026-08-01, three weeks after the cancellation request
dispute_reason: Buyer was charged for a subscription they explicitly asked the agent to cancel three weeks earlier
gold_rationale: Clear purchasing-agent failure: the cancellation instruction was received and logged, but the agent's tool call failed without any error handling or user notification. Full refund of the renewal charge; flag the agent's cancellation tool as needing failure-detection and retry logic.
